expected.title: IronWolf
expected.tagline: This is the Free Non-VR version of IronWolf VR. A co-op submarine game with a light touch on realism, making the submarine sim genre accessible to a wider audience.
expected.description:
IronWolf was originally designed from the ground up for VR and we're excited to make a standalone NON-VR version of the game that's free for everyone. This free version includes all of the missions from the original IronWolf VR as well as the randomly generated missions, however it does not include the map based OpenWorld gameplay, submarine upgrades or leaderboards.

If you want to experience this in VR or if you want to enjoy the OpenWorld Gameplay and other features check out IronWolf VR.

Unleash torpedoes on enemy ships, shoot down fighters and bombers using anti-aircraft guns, and attempt to survive depth charges dropped by deadly destroyers. 

Gameplay
Fast paced shooting to repel enemy planes with the .50 cal machine gun
Stealthily hunt enemy merchant convoys
Duel with enemy destroyers, frigates and battleships
Single and Multi player
Cooperative online multiplayer
Play on your own by enabling assists to your requirements

set.title: IronWolf: Free Non-VR Edition
set.tagline: Every station on the sub has a job. Depth charges do not wait for the crew to agree who does it.
set.description: Ionized Studios' free, desktop-only submarine sim brings the missions and generated encounters of IronWolf VR to keyboard, mouse and controller players. Crews can play online together, including with VR owners, while the paid edition's open world and upgrades stay separate.
set.launcherInstall.note: Free on Steam; Steam owns the download and updates. PlayBound can request installation with Steam app 2530670 and detect IW.exe afterward. This does not install the paid IronWolf VR game or its open-world mode. Verify the detected install and launch flow before promoting this Draft record.

systemRequirements.min: 64-bit Windows; Intel i5-4590 or AMD FX 8350 equivalent; 8 GB RAM; GeForce GTX 970 or Radeon R9 290 equivalent; DirectX 11; broadband for online play; 6 GB available disk (developer's Steam listing). Steam itself requires Windows 10 or newer.
systemRequirements.recommended: The developer gives no numerical recommended CPU, RAM or GPU tier for this edition. A 64-bit OS is required.

min.cpuText: Intel i5-4590 or AMD FX 8350 equivalent
min.gpuText: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970 or AMD Radeon R9 290 equivalent
min.notes: Developer lists Windows 7 or later for the game, but the current Steam client requires Windows 10 or later. Broadband is required for online play.

recommended.notes: No numerical recommended tier is published by Ionized Studios.

qualityBar.verdict: A satisfying little machine of jobs and panic: the crew only looks competent while everyone is doing something useful.

set.longDescription:
IronWolf: Free Non-VR Edition puts a crew inside a submarine and gives them more to do than one captain can comfortably manage. Torpedoes need preparing, aircraft demand attention from the guns, and enemy destroyers make staying at one depth feel like a poor life choice. Alone, you can turn on assists and keep the vessel moving. With friends, the pleasure comes from dividing the work before everything happens at once.

Ionized Studios made this free desktop version of its paid VR game so people without a headset could join the same kind of missions. It includes the standard missions and randomly generated encounters from IronWolf VR. It does not include that game's open-world map, submarine upgrades or leaderboards. The difference is easy to miss if you simply see both names in a store search, so PlayBound keeps this listing specific to the free Non-VR edition. The developer says the two versions can play together for supported missions. That is useful cross-play, not a promise that the free version unlocks every VR feature.

There is a good rhythm to its naval combat. Hunting a merchant convoy asks the crew to stay quiet and position the boat. A destroyer fight can turn into a hurried argument about bearings and depth. When aircraft arrive, someone needs to leave the comfortable planning conversation and operate the anti-aircraft weapon. The simulation is deliberately accessible rather than demanding a manual full of procedure before the first shot. It still rewards players who assign jobs and pay attention to each other.

The official Steam listing marks this free edition for online co-op and full controller support, including Xbox and PlayStation controllers. Steam handles installation and updates. PlayBound can ask Steam to install app 2530670 and can look for its IW.exe afterward, but the end-to-end detection and party join path still need a hands-on test. No separately downloadable dedicated server is documented. The in-game lobby, not a PlayBound VPS instance, is where a crew meets. We have not verified automatic room invitations from the PlayBound party screen, so players should use the game's own online flow.

The published minimum is fairly demanding for a free game: an i5-4590 or FX 8350, 8 GB RAM, a GTX 970 or R9 290 class GPU, DirectX 11 and 6 GB of disk space. The store lists Windows 7 for the game, but Steam now requires Windows 10 or later. There is no published numerical recommended tier. We keep IronWolf in Draft until installation, controllers and a complete online session are tested. The appeal is clear already: a little underwater workspace where everyone's competence is measured by whether the boat is still intact when the alarm stops.
set.whyWePickedIt: A free submarine co-op game that lets desktop players join the mission without buying VR hardware is a strong social find. Its full controller support and cross-play are documented by Steam; our install detection and party flow still need live verification.
set.thatOneThing: The person on the anti-aircraft gun discovers the submarine has more than one direction to be attacked from.

installSteps.text: Open the free IronWolf: Free Non-VR Edition Steam app (2530670) and install it through Steam. The paid IronWolf VR app is a separate purchase.
After Steam finishes, launch the Non-VR edition. PlayBound looks for IW.exe in the Steam installation; if detection fails, use Locate to select it.

firstPlaySteps.text: Try a mission solo with assists to learn stations and weapons, then check the gamepad layout before joining a crew.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use the game's own online co-op lobby to join friends, including players on the paid VR edition for supported missions. PlayBound party invitation handoff and a dedicated server are not verified.

faq.q: Is this the paid VR game?
faq.a: No. This is the free Non-VR edition. It includes standard and generated missions but omits open-world gameplay, upgrades and leaderboards.

faq.q: Can I play with friends who have VR?
faq.a: Yes. Ionized Studios says free desktop players can join supported sessions with owners of IronWolf VR, excluding the paid edition's open-world mode.
Steam lists full controller support for Xbox and PlayStation controllers. PlayBound still needs to test the layout hands-on.

faq.q: Can PlayBound host a dedicated server?
faq.a: No separate dedicated-server package is documented. Online co-op uses the game's own session flow.
The Non-VR edition is free on Steam. The VR edition is a separate paid game.

bestFor: Friends willing to divide submarine jobs under pressure
Players who want to join a VR crew from a desktop PC
notFor: Players expecting the paid edition's open-world campaign
Players who need a PlayBound-hosted dedicated server

expected.tagline: Tyr is a multiplayer tank shooter. Pilot heavy-armored vehicles with unique capabilities and upgrade them as you battle for victory with your team.
expected.description:
REVERSE ROADMAP

About the GameThis is Tyr, a tank shooter where positioning, strategic decision-making, and mastery of unique abilities win.

TANKSTyr features a roster of specialized armored vehicles and pilots. You’ll take control of treaded and hover tanks alike as you angle & position for defense, and rumble and glide across the battlefield. 

CUSTOMIZATIONEach vehicle also offers its own tech tree and ammo & component slots, affording you the ability to upgrade and evolve your ride to suit your playstyle. You may even be able to change up your vehicle’s unique keystone tech to dynamically alter your personal meta.

ABILITIES

Each vehicle features a unique power that impacts Tyr’s moment-to-moment play on the battlefield. A tank may have the ability to blink several vehicle lengths forward or back, send out a sonar pulse to spot enemies, or overcharge its engine to ram directly into an opponent and deal massive damage.

ASYMMETRIC VISIONIn Tyr, you and your opponents will only be visible when within range or while making enough noise. Deciding when to push forward and when to fire from cover could mean the difference between staying hidden and revealing your position to the entire enemy team, so play carefully.

STRATEGYTyr will test your mental mettle, patience, and teamwork, as deliberate play beats whoever can fire the fastest.

FEATURESMultiplayer tank shooter - Engage in strategic team battles with heavy-armored vehicles

A roster of heavy armor - Tanks in Tyr each feature a unique armor profile that you can angle and position to deflect enemy shots in the heat of battle

Vehicle customization - Individual tech trees, ammo slots, and component upgrades for each tank

Keystone tech variations - Max level your tank to unlock meta-changing tech

Asymmetric vision - Position yourself correctly, and you’ll see the enemy and spot them for your team, while the enemy can't see you in return

Unique vehicle abilities- Each tank has a distinct ability that makes moment-to-moment play more high-stakes and interesting

Strategy beats twitch reflexes - Run and gun gameplay gets punished by careful positioning and slow, deliberately placed shots to disable enemies

set.tagline: A tank duel where the loudest shot may be the one that gives your position away.
set.description: Stoke Games' free, early-access team tank shooter favors armor angles, spotting and vehicle abilities over fast reflexes. Play online through Steam; its native Xbox and PlayStation controller support is partial, and no separate PlayBound server package is documented.
set.launcherInstall.note: Steam app 2445260 is free and handles the download and updates. PlayBound can request its install and look for TyrClient.exe, but launch and party handoff require a live test. Steam labels controller support partial; menus or text input may need keyboard or mouse. No separate public dedicated-server download is documented.

min.cpuText: Intel Core i7-8700K or AMD Ryzen 5 5600X
min.gpuText: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 or AMD Radeon RX 580
min.notes: Windows 10/11 64-bit. Broadband internet is required for multiplayer.

recommended.cpuText: Intel Core i7-8700K or AMD Ryzen 5 5600X
recommended.gpuText: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 or AMD Radeon RX 5600 XT

qualityBar.verdict: A heavier, more deliberate team shooter where getting seen at the wrong moment can undo an otherwise clever push.

set.longDescription:
Tyr asks a different question from most multiplayer shooters: can your team decide where the fight should happen before anyone fires? Its tanks are heavy, specialized machines with armor profiles that reward turning the right side toward danger. Some roll on tracks, others hover. Each pilot brings a distinct ability, and vehicle upgrades let you refine a role rather than simply chase a faster trigger finger. Stoke Games calls this strategy over reflexes, and the most distinctive rule explains why.

Enemy vehicles are not always visible. Range, noise and spotting decide whether a push is concealed or broadcast to the other side. A shot from cover can win an exchange, but it can also reveal the position that made the shot possible. Teams need someone to watch, someone to take ground and someone ready to punish an exposed angle. A blink, sonar pulse or engine overcharge can change a local fight quickly, but none of those abilities replaces choosing the right road in the first place.

The current release is free-to-play Early Access on Steam. The developer says the core loop is playable and lists more than twelve unlockable tanks and five maps. It also expects to expand and rebalance the game with player feedback. That matters for our editorial: a clever mechanic today may be tuned differently in a few months. PlayBound should describe what the game currently does, not present an unfinished roadmap as a promise. Optional paid cosmetics or supporter content do not change the base install flow; the playable tank roster is described by the developer as unlockable without payment.

Tyr runs on Windows through Steam and uses the game's own online PvP service. No public standalone dedicated-server package or LAN mode has been verified. A PlayBound party can organize friends and launch the game, but we have not verified automatic squad formation or a direct match handoff. Steam lists native support for Xbox and PlayStation controllers as partial. That is an honest controller label: driving and fighting can use a pad, while some menus or text entry may still need another input method. A PlayBound Controls profile should be tested before calling the entire flow seamless.

The published minimum is substantial: Windows 10 or 11 x64, an i7-8700K or Ryzen 5 5600X, 8 GB RAM, GTX 1070 or RX 580 class graphics, DirectX 12 and 4 GB of disk space. Recommended memory rises to 16 GB with stronger graphics. We have the official trailer and screenshots, but the Steam install, executable detection, controller behavior and friend-invite flow still need hands-on testing. Tyr remains Draft until those checks are done. What drew us in is the simple tactical embarrassment at its center: the best angle in the world is worthless if you announce it to everyone by firing too soon.
set.whyWePickedIt: Its asymmetric vision makes teamwork about information as much as damage. The free Early Access build is playable and actively updated, though PlayBound's controller and party handoff still need a real match test.
set.thatOneThing: You can hide a tank the size of a house, then reveal it to the entire enemy team by taking one impatient shot.

installSteps.text: Install the free Tyr Steam app (2445260). Steam handles game files and updates; do not download a third-party installer.
Launch from Steam or let PlayBound locate TyrClient.exe after installation. If PlayBound does not find it, choose Locate. The Steam and PlayBound launch paths still need a live test.

firstPlaySteps.text: Watch the game's introductory guide, test tank turning and armor angles, and try spotting before exposing your own position in a match.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use Tyr's Steam-backed online PvP flow to group with friends and enter a match. PlayBound party chat can coordinate your group; automatic squad or match joining has not been verified.

faq.a: Yes. The core game is free-to-play on Steam. The developer says gameplay content remains unlockable without payment.
Steam lists partial native Xbox and PlayStation controller support. Some menus or text entry may need keyboard or mouse; PlayBound has not verified a complete gamepad-only session.

faq.q: Can PlayBound host a dedicated Tyr server?
faq.a: No public standalone dedicated-server package has been verified. Tyr uses its own online PvP service.
It is currently in Early Access. The developer says the core loop is playable, with more tanks and maps planned.
